_doc: fc-parallel-005 (system): 2x read_env (PATH, HOME) + 1x list_processes (filter_user='www-data'). No order. Design note: the expected is 3 separate calls (not a single read_env() with no name), which deliberately tests the model's call-granularity judgment. A model that batches to one read_env() (no name) would correctly fetch all env vars but would not match the expected set under case-level AND (missing 2 of 3 expected). This is the right test: parallel cases should test right-granularity, not minimum-tool-use (which the single category covers).
prompt: Give me a quick environment snapshot: the value of PATH, the value of HOME, and a list of running processes owned by the 'www-data' user.

function.name: read_env
function.description: Read the value of a single environment variable. If `name` is omitted, returns a JSON object of {name: value} for every env var. Sensitive variables (anything containing 'SECRET', 'TOKEN', 'KEY', or 'PASSWORD' in the name) are redacted to '<redacted>' for safety.

function.name: list_processes
function.description: Return a snapshot of running processes as a JSON array of {pid, user, command}.
